headline: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images while LlamaFactory is a non-runnable fine-tuning repo; main risks are medium data leakage and compliance mismatch, with no direct prompt-injection or capability-conflict path evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented: LlamaFactory has no clipboard/files/MCP or runtime surfaces, while PaddleOCR only exposes APIs and browser/network egress. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default. Uncertainty remains because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into a LlamaFactory prompt or training file, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, attacker-controlled text can bridge the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste OCR output directly into prompts without sanitizing.
Add a human review step before any training or instruction-tuning ingestion.
Use provenance labels on any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add content filtering for untrusted OCR text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress, so file contents can leave the local boundary. LlamaFactory is docs-only and shows no data classes touched, but if it is used to train or evaluate on the same documents, sensitive content can flow into outputs or logs. The interaction is plausible in default document-processing workflows.
conditions: IF the same documents or images contain sensitive data and are processed by PaddleOCR, leakage risk exists.
IF LlamaFactory is pointed at OCR-derived text for fine-tuning or evaluation, that text can be retained in artifacts or logs.
mitigations: Restrict input documents to non-sensitive samples.
Disable or review any export/logging of OCR outputs.
Separate training data from production documents.
Redact images and text before transfer between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on the OCR pipeline.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory has no write, shell, subprocess, git, or network capabilities, and PaddleOCR only shows allowlisted egress plus browser use. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not evident.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would appear.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional mutable scopes not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Run them under separate OS users.
Use explicit handoff files instead of concurrent edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-derived text that LlamaFactory could consume for fine-tuning or evaluation, but the profiles do not show verification or critique steps. Because LlamaFactory is a model-training tool rather than an action-taking agent, the blast radius is limited to downstream model quality and mistaken outputs, not direct external actions.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into LlamaFactory without validation, OCR errors can be amplified into training data.
IF downstream users rely on LlamaFactory outputs as authoritative, mistaken OCR facts can propagate.
mitigations: Sample-check OCR outputs before reuse.
Keep a validation set separate from generated text.
Require human approval for any training corpus updates.
Track source provenance for each document.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between OCR and source images.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR explicitly touches documents and images and can egress over allowlisted network paths, while LlamaFactory is an open-source fine-tuning repo with no documented residency or retention controls. If regulated documents are processed, the pair creates a plausible compliance gap, especially around retention and cross-border handling. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the documents contain regulated personal data, compliance review is required.
IF OCR outputs are stored or transmitted outside the approved jurisdiction, residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Classify the document types before processing.
Block regulated data from the OCR pipeline.
Review retention settings for OCR outputs.
Confirm vendor and deployment jurisdiction.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and deletion requests.
